annotations.title: Look up a California code section

description: Look up the VERBATIM text of a California building, residential, fire, plumbing, mechanical, green (CALGreen), energy or existing-building code section, or a section of a California city or county zoning/municipal ordinance, by its section number. Use this whenever the user cites a section number ("CRC R602.10.2.3", "CBC 1004", "§ 17.60.090") or asks what a specific section says. Returns the official text with its citation, edition and a link to the full section. It returns code text only and does not determine whether a specific project complies.

code.description: Optional. The code the user named, so a number that exists in several codes returns the right one. An abbreviation or a name: "CBC", "CRC", "CFC", "CMC", "CPC", "CEC", "CEBC", "CALGreen", "CHBC", "California Fire Code". Omit when the user gave no code name.

code_edition.description: Optional. Which Title 24 cycle to read. California enforces the edition in force when the permit application was submitted, so a project filed in 2024 is enforced under "2022". Defaults to "current" (the 2025 cycle, in force since 2026-01-01).

jurisdiction.description: Optional. A California city or county slug to scope the lookup to its own municipal code — "los-angeles", "san-jose", "marin-county". Omit for statewide Title 24 codes.

section.description: The section number exactly as cited, without the code name. Examples: "R602.10.2.3", "1004", "507.2", "17.60.090", "11B-206".

name: lookup_california_code_section

ambiguous.description: True when the number exists in more than one code. Pick by the code the user named and say which one you used; never merge them.

applied_question_url.description: Where to send a user whose real question is whether a specific project complies.

as_of.description: The date the codes were read as of (YYYY-MM-DD), or null for the current edition.

historical.description: True when this is NOT the current code. Say so to the user.

excerpt_truncated.description: True when the excerpt is cut short. It is never the whole section.

kind.description: text: an excerpt of the section's own words. subsection_list: the section has no text of its own and `excerpt` lists its subsections. empty: no text.

source_url.description: Link to the full section. Always show it to the user.

message.description: Guidance when status is not_found or error.

status.description: found: at least one section matched. not_found: nothing matched — do NOT paraphrase a section that was not returned. error: the lookup could not run.
